correctness.rationale: Use ranks of independent continuous random variables to identify uniform cyclic permutation comparisons. Independently enumerated all 3!,4!,5! local orderings, obtaining joint moments (P_0P_d,P_0V_d)=(1/3,0),(0,5/24),(2/15,11/120) for d=0,1,2. The resulting block-circulant A,B kernels are exact for every n>=5, including n=5 because distances 1 and 2 are distinct. Fourier block channels have positive plus band (19-5c+2c^2)/180 and minus band (1-c)(3-2c)/12, whose only zero at c=1 corresponds to the telescoping peak-minus-valley conservation. Both band polynomials decrease in c; comparing minus first frequency with plus minimum 4/45 yields n=5 exception and n>=6 sharp condition formula. The asymptotic 5/pi^2 n^2 follows from Taylor expansion of 1-cos(2pi/n); peak-only spectrum tends to condition 11. No extrapolation from the finite verification is used.

originality.rationale: Bandt (2022) studies aggregated consecutive ordinal-pattern turning rates and long-run covariances, including aggregate peak/valley constraints; those are not new. Overlap-count methods of Crane–DeSalvo–Elizalde and Fu's peaks are prior. Published six-triple-pattern aggregate covariance tables concern a fixed-dimensional total-count vector, not all spatial modes in the 2n-position cyclic covariance. Resultary returned no mathematically dominating finite cyclic two-channel spectrum. Thus the precise n-resolved rank, band branches and sharp n^2 conditioning pass best-of-knowledge O with unindexed cyclic point-process priority risk.
